title: Lipschitz derivative of a Gaussian indicator average
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $u\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sin u\ne0$. Define $v_u(x)=\int 1_A(\cos u\,x+\sin u\,Y)\,d\gamma_n(Y)$ for standard Gaussian $Y$. The derivative map $x\mapsto Dv_u(x)$ is Lipschitz with constant $2n^2/\sin^2u$, using the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$ and the operator norm on linear functionals.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable and $\sin u\ne0$, then $x\mapsto D u_u(x)$ is globally $2n^2/\sin^2u$-Lipschitz in operator norm for the maximum norm on $\mathbb R^n$.
